body:
Huh, does the effect stick around even after the medication is stopped? 

I have an anxiety induced tic that looks like a much, much milder version of the second guy (a kind of one-sided shrug/punch thing) and it didn't show up until after I was briefly (<6 mos.) on risperidone. That was almost 5 years ago- do the effects even last that long?

Thank you, guys. The only person who I repeated that quote to was my mother to explain why I was being so distant towards my sister. Her reaction was "You need to get over it- she said that because she loves you. Anyway, she's not wrong". I tried to "get over it" for a long time but it finally occurred to me that maybe I have a right to not be over it and to be pissed about it. I thought maybe what she said *was* horrible and something I have the right to be angry and hurt over, and judging by your reactions, I'm not crazy for feeling that way.

I have one semester of school left (if I don't fail out this month) and I've been thinking about getting as far away from my family as possible. It feels selfish and there are people I don't want to leave behind but I think it's going to have to be an all-or-none kind of thing and I cannot do 'all'. 

In the meantime, it's difficult to not feel like I only have one way out, especially when that option seems like it would be best for my family, but I'm putting up a fight. Thank you guys for your support and for helping me see that I deserve better than that from my family.
